narrative.overview:
The website is a quiet, dark product stage that begins almost empty and assembles Izge's role in front of the visitor: mark, documents, relationships, conversation, and a qualified finding. The opening keeps the relationship graph unlabeled, marks the `@izge` mention, thinks for two seconds, and streams the reply for two seconds without playback controls. It then moves through four product chapters—company memory, finding, customer-response draft, and scheduled review—before native scroll carries a reversible team exchange into a closing invitation.

This is a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript expression of the Izge identity. It preserves the real mark, bundled Cambay and Inter type, grounded fixture data, rendered source disclosure, and message anatomy. Every apparent AI or operational state uses deterministic local fixtures; the walkthrough does not send a message, contact a customer, create an invoice, or call a model.

The earlier finding-first discovery composition remains a historical exploration, not the current implemented layout. The current code-led motion experience is the source of truth; no raster composition defines its structure.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black teal canvas with restrained blue and warm review accents.
Cambay statements paired with practical Inter interface text and the Izge mark.
A control-free 12-second blank-to-built opening with two seconds of thinking and a two-second streamed reply.
Reload-only scroll and hash reset while ordinary deep links retain their destination.
Four reversible native-scroll chapters with sequential daily-review rows and readable stacked fallbacks.
An initially empty, scroll-pinned `@izge` playback whose full composer becomes a right-aligned You/Siz self-message.
Velocity-assisted streaming, scroll-gated colleague reactions, reverse removal/unstreaming, and pause/replay team controls without a redundant secondary heading.
A rising, growing closing composition with demo and `mailto:alperkartkaya@gmail.com` contact actions.
EN/TR parity, safely rendered bundled Markdown, and explicit human authority boundaries.

rules.name: The Warmth Requires Review Rule
rules.body: Warm text means “look closer and decide,” never “revenue recovered” or “work completed.”

rules.name: The Evidence Before Superlatives Rule
rules.body: Display copy states what Izge connects or prepares; it does not claim autonomous recovery, certainty, or a completed customer outcome.

rules.name: The Same Story at Every Size Rule
rules.body: Responsive changes may stack, tighten, or unpin the composition, but they preserve all four chapters, source access, team/private views, the complete fixture answer, and human-review qualification.

rules.name: The Evidence Stays Grounded Rule
rules.body: Resting product and evidence surfaces use borders and tonal layers, not promotional shadows.

dos: **Do** preserve the real Izge mark, the established dark palette, and the Cambay/Inter pairing.
**Do** keep EN/TR content structurally equivalent and test both languages for overflow.
**Do** use fixture-grounded documents and keep source access keyboard-operable and focus-restoring.
**Do** keep deterministic fixture behavior testable and keep customer confirmation, commercial approval, and human review explicit.
**Do** show the complete final state for reduced motion and the readable stacked chapter fallback at 500px viewport height or less.
**Do** keep functional text at 11px or larger.
donts: **Don't** treat an earlier raster or discovery composition as the current layout authority; the implemented HTML, CSS, and JavaScript define this implemented experience.
**Don't** present thinking or streaming as a live model response.
**Don't** imply the page sends a message, contacts a customer, creates an invoice, or executes any other external action.
**Don't** mark the potential amount as recovered revenue, a finalized receivable, or an approved invoice.
**Don't** let Izge make the commercial decision; a responsible employee reviews and approves the next step.
**Don't** introduce integration logos, invented metrics, unsupported source formats, decorative glow, or motion without a complete static equivalent.
